best_moment.what: Confessing to the Telegram leak and then the inquiry not finding me, with a hidden clock of about eleven years hanging over me. It was the one moment that felt like a real BitLife-style consequence.

worst_moment.what: Another year of picking B (be seen) with no visible change and no politics invitation. It felt like grinding a stat I couldn't see, with nothing happening.

skip_year.why: It was one of the repeated 'be seen' years between Y34 and Y37 where nothing moved. I could have skipped straight to Y38 and lost nothing.

CEP went up, and I reached the top grade, which felt like a direct result.
Padded bids worked at Y28 and Y33, so the lesson came back as a rule I could use.

answer.held_back_by: STAND stayed at 50 the whole time, probably because of all the candour, and I think that is what stopped the politics invitation. Or the game simply never offers politics unless you pick one hidden thing, and I never found out what it was.
answer.ending_fair_why: I reached the top rung with max integrity and then retired with an ending card that said nothing about the leak, the MP, or the politics invitation I'd spent years working towards. The setups were promised and never paid off, so it felt like a flat ending rather than an unfair one.
answer.chase_next: The politics route. I want to see the invitation, the MP callback, and what 'a different life' actually looks like, since this run never showed me any of it.
answer.play_again_why: I want to see whether the politics path exists and whether the callbacks actually pay off. I'd pick the ambitious options and skip the repeated 'be seen' grind.

tone_breaks.line: No street is named after you and none ever will be, which is rather the point.
tone_breaks.note: It's a knowing, slightly clever line on the ending card that nudges the reader. It's mild, but it does wink.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is about slow career steps, grades and appraisals, so 'Confirmed & Substantive' sounds like the right kind of job language. 'Minister Salary' suggests a big payoff at the top, and I never got to politics or a minister's pay.
